```
• 有，但不是完整一對一的官方 gh notifications 子命令。

  最接近的是：

  gh status

  它會列出跨 repo 的 assigned issues、PRs、review requests、mentions、repo activity / notifications。官方 manual 也把 gh status 描述成顯示 issues、PRs 和 notifications 的狀態。來源：gh status
  (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_reference)

  如果你要等價於 https://github.com/notifications inbox，比較實用的是直接打 GitHub REST API：

  gh api --method GET notifications --paginate \
    --jq '.[] | "\(.id) [\(.reason)] \(.repository.full_name): \(.subject.title)"'

  常用操作：

  # 只看參與或被 mention 的通知
  gh api --method GET notifications -F participating=true --paginate

  # 包含已讀
  gh api --method GET notifications -F all=true --paginate

  # 標記單一 thread 為 read
  gh api --method PATCH notifications/threads/THREAD_ID

  # 標記單一 thread 為 done
  gh api --method DELETE notifications/threads/THREAD_ID

  # 全部標為 read
  gh api --method PUT notifications -f read=true

  GitHub 官方 REST docs 有列 notifications list/read/done endpoints。來源：GitHub REST notifications (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/activity/notifications?apiVersion=2022-11-28)

  如果想要 TUI，社群 extension 有 gh notify：

  gh ext install sideshowbarker/gh-notify
  gh notify

  這類 extension 更像網頁版 inbox，可以互動瀏覽和標 done。來源：sideshowbarker/gh-notify (https://sideshowbarker.net/gh-notify/)

  另外你本機已經裝了 gh dash，它偏 PR / issue dashboard，也可以輔助處理通知，但不是 notification inbox 的完全替代。

  if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && [[ -f "$_REPO_ROOT/.pre-commit-config.yaml" ]]; then

  # tldr cache
  if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then

  fi

  # gh extensions
  if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    info "Upgrading gh extensions"
    _run gh extension upgrade --all || any_fail=1
    ran_any=1
  fi

  if [[ "$ran_any" -eq 0 ]]; then
    warn "no plugin managers detected — skipping"
    return $SKIP_RC
  fi
  return "$any_fail"

I now have the full picture. Let me answer both questions.

## Short answer

**1. Updating gh extensions (incl. gh-dash) — already wired into this repo.** You don't need to run the raw `gh` command; there's a managed recipe:

```bash
just upgrade-plugins      # LazyVim + TPM + claude-hud + pre-commit + tldr + gh extensions
```

Under the hood (`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh:872`) it runs:

```bash
gh extension upgrade --all
```

Or just do the one-off directly for gh-dash:

```bash
gh extension upgrade dlvhdr/gh-dash   # → v4.23.2 to latest
# or: gh extension upgrade --all
```

This fits the repo's **install-vs-upgrade split** invariant: `chezmoi apply` + ansible only *installs* gh-dash (`gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash`, guarded so it never re-runs); upgrades are explicit via `just upgrade-*`. So the "Update available!" banner is expected drift — the box installs, `upgrade-plugins` bumps.

**2. Should you set up `gh notify`?**

My recommendation: **yes, but only if you'll actually use the notifications inbox in the terminal.** Here's the honest tradeoff versus what you already have:

| Tool | Role | Already managed? |
|---|---|---|
| `gh dash` | PR/issue **dashboard** (custom section queries) | ✅ ansible-installed + `upgrade-plugins` |
| `gh notify` | Notifications **inbox** (the `github.com/notifications` equivalent, interactive mark-read/done) | ❌ not installed |
| `gh status` / `gh api notifications` | one-shot CLI, no TUI | built-in |

`gh dash` and `gh notify` don't really overlap — dash is "what needs my attention across queries," notify is "my actual inbox threads." If you regularly triage the web notifications inbox, `gh notify` earns its place.

**Note:** the correct repo is `meiji163/gh-notify` (the search result's `sideshowbarker` attribution was wrong). Install: `gh extension install meiji163/gh-notify`.

## 1. gh-dash ansible install block — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (lines ~1188–1222)

The block is 4 tasks under the `# --- gh-dash ---` comment:

```yaml
# --- gh-dash ---
- name: Check if gh is available for gh-dash extension installation
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v gh
  register: gh_cli_path
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Check if gh is authenticated
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0
  ansible.builtin.command: gh auth status
  register: gh_auth_status
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: List installed gh extensions
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0
  ansible.builtin.command: gh extension list
  register: gh_extension_list
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Install gh-dash extension
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0 and (gh_extension_list.rc != 0 or 'dlvhdr/gh-dash' not in gh_extension_list.stdout)
  ansible.builtin.command: gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
  changed_when: true
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
```

**Reuse question (important):** `gh_cli_path`, `gh_auth_status`, and `gh_extension_list` are each registered **once**. `gh_extension_list` captures the full `gh extension list` stdout, so a new gh-notify install task can **reuse the existing `gh_extension_list` register directly** — no new list/auth/path tasks are needed. A single new task mirroring the "Install gh-dash extension" task suffices, e.g. guarded on `... and (gh_extension_list.rc != 0 or 'meiji163/gh-notify' not in gh_extension_list.stdout)` with `gh extension install meiji163/gh-notify`. The three probe tasks are generic (not gh-dash-specific), so placing the new install task anywhere after `List installed gh extensions` works.

---
# Developer CLI tools role
# Tools: bat, bats, gh, glab, diffnav, gh-dash, eza, git-delta, git-graph, tldr, glow, gum, vhs, freeze, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, superfile, tmux, sesh, worktrunk, workmux, zellij, herdr, btop, htop, duckdb, rclone, coreutils, taplo, television, pandoc, tailspin, lnav, grc, ccze (Linux only), dasel, yq, jnv, witr, figlet, toilet, lolcat, fastfetch

# =============================================================================
# macOS - all via Homebrew
    - name: Clean up diffnav (user) temp files after failure
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz
        - /tmp/diffnav-extract

# --- gh-dash ---
- name: Check if gh is available for gh-dash extension installation
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v gh
  register: gh_cli_path
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Check if gh is authenticated
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0
  ansible.builtin.command: gh auth status
  register: gh_auth_status
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: List installed gh extensions
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0
  ansible.builtin.command: gh extension list
  register: gh_extension_list
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Install gh-dash extension
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0 and (gh_extension_list.rc != 0 or 'dlvhdr/gh-dash' not in gh_extension_list.stdout)
  ansible.builtin.command: gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
  changed_when: true
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

# --- git-graph ---
# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — git-graph is a
# Rust musl binary (no glibc dependency). x86_64-only by upstream choice.
- name: Check if git-graph is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
  ansible.builtin.command: git-graph --version
  register: git_graph_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
```

## 1. gh-dash ansible install block — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (lines ~1188–1222)

The block is 4 tasks under the `# --- gh-dash ---` comment:

```yaml
# --- gh-dash ---
- name: Check if gh is available for gh-dash extension installation
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v gh
  register: gh_cli_path
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Check if gh is authenticated
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0
  ansible.builtin.command: gh auth status
  register: gh_auth_status
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: List installed gh extensions
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0
  ansible.builtin.command: gh extension list
  register: gh_extension_list
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Install gh-dash extension
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0 and (gh_extension_list.rc != 0 or 'dlvhdr/gh-dash' not in gh_extension_list.stdout)
  ansible.builtin.command: gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
  changed_when: true
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
```

**Reuse question (important):** `gh_cli_path`, `gh_auth_status`, and `gh_extension_list` are each registered **once**. `gh_extension_list` captures the full `gh extension list` stdout, so a new gh-notify install task can **reuse the existing `gh_extension_list` register directly** — no new list/auth/path tasks are needed. A single new task mirroring the "Install gh-dash extension" task suffices, e.g. guarded on `... and (gh_extension_list.rc != 0 or 'meiji163/gh-notify' not in gh_extension_list.stdout)` with `gh extension install meiji163/gh-notify`. The three probe tasks are generic (not gh-dash-specific), so placing the new install task anywhere after `List installed gh extensions` works.
